audience.programmeDescription: Psychology at UvA studies behaviour and mental processes through research, statistics and broad psychological foundations. This example follows the Brain and Cognition specialisation, with named current topics on consciousness and AI, an empirical thesis and thirty credits of open choice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines broad psychology with neuroscience, cognition and empirical data methods. Two further options emphasise clinical and health questions or social behaviour and organisations. UvA provides a more prescribed disciplinary and specialist practical sequence; the partial relationships do not reproduce its required thesis or confer clinical qualification.

componentNotes.y1-07: Academic-skills practicals and research participation are compulsory without additional credits. All earlier reading and writing assignments must be passed before the first-year thesis.

componentNotes.y2-08: The 12-EC toolbox integrates behavioural experiments, neuroscience methods, data analysis, experimental design and Python programming.
componentNotes.y3-01: Entry requires the full first year, Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least 18 EC of the specialisation, including its toolbox. All are completed in Year 2.
componentNotes.y3-02: The 12-EC empirical thesis follows the first part of Behavioural Research Toolbox. The earlier requirements and at least 18 specialisation credits must be passed. Five colloquium points must also be obtained; they add no separate degree credits. Students conduct supervised group research and write individual empirical reports.

componentNotes.y3-04: Selected from the restricted period-two Current Topics menu: the relationship between psychological science and AI. The full first year is required; prior AI or programming knowledge is not.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD111.name: Personal Leadership
BENLEAD111.text: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.

BENLEAD112.name: Leadership Communication
BENLEAD112.text: Studies leadership communication through theory, persuasion, emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Students analyse literary characters, film and speeches, interview a leader, prepare a communication advisory report, and develop an address explaining their own ethical leadership vision.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

BENLEAD312.text: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.

Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
